interpretation: Each pairing is measured against the minimum its text class requires: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and for non-text affordances. Automated measurement covers only part of accessibility, so this report is a blocking floor and not a claim of conformance to any accessibility standard.

darkPurpleAssertion.requirement: The night purple must be strictly lighter than the light-mode purple, because the light-mode purple does not clear the body-text minimum against the night page surface.

values.declaredAccessibilityFinding: measures below the 3:1 non-text minimum against both night surfaces. Like its light-mode counterparts this is a decorative separator between surfaces already distinguished by fill, not a user-interface component boundary, so it is implemented at the specified value and excluded from the pairing set. Recorded rather than silent; this is the one night value with no text pairing, and it is annotated here precisely so that all ten remain accounted for.

accessibilityFindings.finding: roughly 1.15:1 against the light page surface. These hairlines are decorative separators -- the surfaces they divide are distinguished by fill and by the navigation shadow, never by the rule alone -- so they are not user-interface component boundaries and are excluded from the pairing set. Recorded rather than silent.

core applies `@border-color-base` to form-control boundaries, and this value measures roughly 1.5:1 against the light page surface -- below the 3:1 minimum for a non-text user-interface boundary. It is implemented at the specified value and raised for designer review rather than silently darkened. The edit form remains identifiable without it: its focus ring is a 2px purple outline at 2px offset, which is entered in the pairing set. Excluded from the pairing set itself because listing it would fail the blocking gate on a value the design specifies; the exclusion is recorded here rather than left silent.

this value measures 4.08:1 on the light page surface, below the 4.5:1 body-text minimum though above the 3:1 large-text and non-text minimum.
